title: How We See
seo_title: Year 6 Science: How We See Worksheets (Ray Diagrams, Reflection and the Eye)
standard_text: Use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain that objects are seen because they give out or reflect light into the eye. Explain that we see things because light travels from light sources to our eyes or from light sources to objects and then to our eyes.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on how we see: light travelling into the eye, ray diagrams, luminous and non-luminous objects, parts of the eye and pupil size. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: We see when light enters our eyes.
key_sub: Light goes from a source, bounces off objects, and travels into the eye.
body_html:
How to think about it

We see things when light enters our eyes.

  • Light sources (luminous): light travels straight from them into our eyes.
  • Other objects: light from a source reflects off them and travels into our eyes.
  • In ray diagrams, arrows go from the source, to the object, to the eye, never out of the eye. With no light at all, we see nothing.
Example

How do you see a book under a lamp?

Lamp → book

Book → eye

Answer: light reflects off the book into your eye

Example

Dark room or bright sunshine: bigger pupil?

Pupils open to let in more light

Answer: dark room

Common mistakes

  • Drawing arrows coming out of the eye.
  • Thinking you can see in total darkness after a while.
  • Thinking objects like the Moon give out their own light.

faq.a: Light from a light source either goes straight into our eyes, or reflects off an object and then travels into our eyes.

faq.q: Which way should arrows point in a ray diagram?
faq.a: From the light source to the object and from the object to the eye, showing the direction light travels. Arrows never come out of the eye.

faq.q: Why can't we see in total darkness?
faq.a: With no light, nothing can reflect into our eyes, so we cannot see anything at all.
